about: The Verdance crashed transport (Grok Bot's Rodin mesh, 32 m) with two fallen-deck-plate ramps up to its ruptured midsection, failing lights and collision. Unreal cm, site-relative; the site pivot is the mesh pivot: on the ground at the centre of the hull. +X is the nose. The ruptured opening goes right through the ship along Y; a ramp on each side.

pieces.name: Wreck
pieces.note: Everything below Z = 0 is the ramp props (40 cm). Material slot 0: the three failing lights under the opening's ceiling are scalar LightPower (0 off, 1 on) x GlowStrength (14) x GlowColor (warm orange). Flicker them by animating LightPower on a dynamic instance.

core_interact.note: There is no modelled core in the mesh: the objective's core pickup goes on the deck at the centre of the opening (deck top Z 252). The pilot faces the nose (+X); the ceiling lights are at site (40, 140, 562), (190, -120, 564) and (-90, -60, 570).

walk_path_site_cm.what: ground in front of the -Y ramp (toe at Y = -992)
on the -Y ramp (20 degrees, 206 cm between the rails)
the deck in the opening (core point)
ground beyond the +Y ramp (toe at Y = +992)

opening_clear_width_along_x.visual_clear: X -75..350 at Z 400 (425); Grok Bot's largest clear rectangle X -56..304 (360)

walkability_cm.deck_lip_as_delivered: 252 at the ramps (Grok Bot measured 276.9 as the lowest edge of the largest clear rectangle); the hanging stairs as delivered drop at 42 degrees to 97 cm above the ground and are covered by the ramps

placement_rules: Put the site pivot ON the ground. Keep 3 m of flat ground beyond each ramp toe (site X -40 to 190, Y -1300 to -992 and 992 to 1300).
Nothing under the hull: it rests on the ground along its length; on slopes sink it up to 40 cm rather than leave the belly floating.
Yaw it freely; never scale it (the opening and the ramps are sized for the 180 cm pilot).
